reason: Confirmed against the installed source and the session transcripts. kaggle 2.2.4 competition_submit_cli (kaggle_api_extended.py l.2026-2036) prints only f'{num_allowed_now} submissions remaining today.' after a submit that did not fail the upload, then returns the server message. For a kernel submit that message is empty, and cli.py prints it with print(out, end=''). Errors are HTTPError, ApiException or ValueError; cli.py prints them to stderr and exits 1 (l.78-103). In the 4 transcript jsonl files, 44 tool results contain 'N submissions remaining today' and none contains 'Successfully submitted'. The only 'Successfully submitted' hit is a notes file quoting R27N text. CONTEXT l.3474 and l.3865 quote the real outputs. So R27N-4's success grep never fires, and R27N-3's 'Expect Successfully submitted' would make the operator misread every success. v2 recovers only because the next pass lists first. That recovery depends on the list showing the new row within 30 s; if the list lagged, v2 would submit the file again and burn a slot, and v3 removes that path. Claim (c) is overstated: the transcripts show Kaggle errors that do carry the status text ('403 Client Error: Forbidden for url', '400 Client Error: Bad Request', '429 Client Error: Too Many Requests'), which come from the raise_for_status branch. Only the JSON-body branch (kagglesdk l.128-131) drops the code. v3 keeps both the word patterns and the code patterns, so this does no harm. My own test of the v3 classifier on 8 realistic strings gave the right class for all 8. The network check runs before the daily-limit check, which matters: 'Max retries exceeded' goes to NETWORK, not DAILY. v3 is ops-only: no effect on the LB or the private score, no runtime cost, and it fails soft (rc 0 without the line = UNKNOWN, then the list runs first). It fits R1-R10 and the night schedule. The residual risk that a 429 daily-limit reply is retried as network is correctly called harmless, because the list-first check blocks a duplicate.
fix: Adopt as written: use night_checklist.md section P nb_try v3 for every night submit, and drop 'Expect Successfully submitted' from all prompts. Two small pointer fixes before the freeze: (1) freeze_line_template.md l.76 says nb_try is in night_checklist.md 'section N', but it is in section P; correct it. (2) The live 00:04Z timer text (timer.sh process) still says 'with the R27N-3 guards'. The freeze line, and the session reading it at 00:04Z, must name night_checklist.md section P (nb_try v3) as the one that applies over R27N-3/R27N-4. Optionally, in the step-3 CONTEXT line, log the 'N submissions remaining today' count as a free used_today cross-check against G2.
realistic_gain: No gain on the LB or the private score. The gain is operational: correct batch logs, no false 'failed' reading at 00:05Z, and no chance of a duplicate submit if the list lags. It costs nothing (no Kaggle calls, no runtime).
